cases.query: Why is the squared L2 norm often mathematically convenient, and what drawback does it have near the origin?
cases.golden_answer: The squared L2 norm is convenient because it can be written as x^T x, and each derivative with respect to an element of x depends only on that corresponding element. Its drawback is that it increases very slowly near the origin, which can be undesirable when small nonzero entries should be distinguished from zero.

cases.query: How does the determinant relate to eigenvalues and to volume expansion or contraction?
cases.golden_answer: The determinant of a square matrix is the product of all of its eigenvalues. The absolute value of the determinant measures how much multiplication by the matrix expands or contracts space. A determinant of 0 means space loses all volume along at least one dimension, while a determinant of 1 preserves volume.
